root.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Muzio Gambit Accepted, From's Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 g4 5. O-O gxf3 6. Qxf3 Qe7

overview: In the Muzio White has played 5.O-O gxf3 6.Qxf3, giving a knight for attack along the f-file and against f7. Black replies 6...Qe7 (From's Defense), covering f7 and preparing to hold the extra piece; White continues with Bxf7+ ideas or Qxf4. Play is very forcing and White has to find a lot of accurate moves; the extra piece should tell if Black defends correctly.

white_ideas.idea: Attack on the f-file with Qxf4 and Bxf7+ ideas
Use development lead with d4, Nc3 and Bxf4

black_ideas.idea: Return material at the right moment and trade queens

typical_structures.structure: Open position with Black king on e8 and White pieces aimed at f7

character.notes: A piece sacrifice with forcing play and mutual attack.

gambit.notes: White has given the knight for a pawn and Black can keep the extra piece.

soundness.notes: The Muzio is widely considered unsound against best defence.

structure.notes: Open lines, with the f-file and e-file in play.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly play it today.

level.notes: Long forcing lines must be known.

character.reason: A piece sacrifice and attack down the f-file make this forcing and double-edged.
